title: How Glaciers Form, Flow and Hold Our Water

post_description: How glaciers form from snow, move downhill and store fresh water, from the USGS and NASA. Sources: United States Geological Survey https://www.usgs.gov/water-science-school/science/glaciers-and-icecaps and National Aeronautics and Space Administration https://science.nasa.gov/kids/earth/10-interesting-things-about-glaciers/ #Science #ScienceFacts #QuantaTale
narration: What is a glacier, and how does one begin? A glacier starts life as snowflakes. When far more snow falls than melts each summer, the weight of the pile compresses the old snow into ice. Gravity pulls the ice downhill so slowly that you would not notice it move. On its way, the ice grinds away at the ground like a gigantic bulldozer. Glaciers cover only a slice of Earth's land, yet they lock up most of its fresh water.
